article_title: Development and validation of a cost-effective DIY simulation model for McDonald cerclage training.
citation: Buechel J, Kalisz A, Herbert S-L, Scherer-Quenzer A, Blau-Schneider B, Starrach T, Kraft K, Wöckel A, Pecks U, Kiesel M. (2024). Development and validation of a cost-effective DIY simulation model for McDonald cerclage training. Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-024-07812-8
title: Wuerzburg Cervical Cerclage Simulator (WCCS)
description: The WCCS is a DIY McDonald cerclage trainer built from a 10 cm drainpipe simulating the vagina, foamed plastic vaginal walls, and two 3D-printed, silicone-duplicated cervix models: a closed cervix for prophylactic cerclage and a cervix "already opened to 1.5 cm with bulging membranes" simulated with a water-filled balloon. It weighs 1110 g, mounts on a desk or examination couch, and cost 39.64 EUR to produce.
requirements: Standard surgical instruments and a light source such as a headlamp or examination light are needed to perform the procedure on the model.
Cervix models must be replaced after multiple uses; each silicone cervix is usable for approximately five to 10 cerclage procedures.
constraints: The WCCS is only suitable for the McDonald technique, not the Shirodkar technique.
The materials do not accurately replicate the haptic properties of cervical and vaginal tissue.
The model was optimized for braided Mersilene sutures and was tested only with them.
target_learners: obstetricians and gynecologists training in McDonald cerclage
target_learning_goals: performing McDonald cerclage stitches for prophylactic and emergency indications
examples: Thirteen obstetricians from four German university hospitals performed McDonald cerclage on the simulator with standard instruments and rated it on a 7-point Likert scale.
key_sources: Buechel J, Kalisz A, Herbert S-L, Scherer-Quenzer A, Blau-Schneider B, Starrach T, Kraft K, Wöckel A, Pecks U, Kiesel M. (2024). Development and validation of a cost-effective DIY simulation model for McDonald cerclage training. Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-024-07812-8

article_title: Key courses of academic curriculum uncovered by data mining of students' grades
citation: L. Gajewski, J. Chołoniewski, J. A. Hołyst. (2016). Key courses of academic curriculum uncovered by data mining of students' grades. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.07074
title: Anonymized grade dataset of 217 applied-physics students across 27 core courses (2010–2015)
description: The dataset was received from the deanery of Faculty of Physics at Warsaw University of Technology and contains final grades, group and specialization records for engineering-degree candidates from 2010 to 2015. After excluding students who did not pass the first five semesters and removing general university courses, 27 core courses remained for three classes (J, K, L). "The total number of students considered in the analyses is 217 (class J – 76 students, K – 66, L – 75)."
requirements: Missing records were filled with the average score at that course across all three classes (6.72% combined)
constraints: Only students who passed the first five semesters were analyzed; missing-grade percentages were 5.46% (J), 14.03% (K), 1.68% (L)
target_learners: undergraduate applied-physics students at Warsaw University of Technology
target_learning_goals: curriculum analysis of physics, mathematics, computer science and electrical engineering core courses
examples: The dataset covers three consecutive classes: J (started 2010), K (2011) and L (2012), represented as a students-by-courses grade matrix for the analyses in the paper.
key_sources: L. Gajewski, J. Chołoniewski, J. A. Hołyst. (2016). Key courses of academic curriculum uncovered by data mining of students' grades. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.07074
